claim: LLM pass-rate distributions on LeetCode problems are bimodal, skewed toward 1.0 (fully correct) and 0.0 (fully failing), attributed to self-consistency bias and outright failure modes rather than a graded spread of partial correctness.
stance_target: Competitive/algorithmic-style code evaluation collapses to near-binary outcomes, in contrast to functional code where partial pass is common
scope_conditions: 18 LLMs, LeetCode dataset, correctness and runtime-efficiency comparison
quoted_support: Solutions are skewed towards pass rates of 1.0 and 0.0, demonstrating a bimodal distribution.
